models.name: Model S — Steady-state Navier–Stokes CFD in tortuous vessel with concentric catheter
models.what_it_computes: Annular pressure drop between vessel wall and catheter shaft, tip-region shear and lateral hydrodynamic side-loads under prescribed steady inflow; QOIs include ΔP across the test segment and tip side-load magnitude

models.name: Model T — Transient CFD with prescribed catheter advancement (moving boundary)
models.what_it_computes: Time-resolved axial drag and lateral hydrodynamic side-load on the advancing catheter tip through curvature and stenosis surrogates; QOIs include cycle-averaged ΔP, peak side-load, and integrated hydrodynamic drag during a standardized push

mechanisms.name: M1 — Axial annular pressure-drop governing flow resistance
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Determines delivered flow at set pump conditions and contributes to insertion force budget relevant for design screening

mechanisms.name: M2 — Dean-type secondary flows causing lateral hydrodynamic side-load at bends
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Side-load can bias catheter tracking over a guidewire in tortuous paths and correlates with steering difficulty

mechanisms.name: M3 — Tip and side-port jetting with local recirculation
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Jet-induced asymmetric forces may perturb guidewire alignment and affect trackability near lesions

mechanisms.name: M4 — Hemorheology-dependent viscosity effects
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Non-Newtonian behavior alters both resistance and shear-driven lateral forces across clinically relevant hematocrit

deviation.detail: All credibility factors are scored on a 0–5 Credibility Index (CI), where 0 = no evidence and 5 = compelling, quantified evidence; CI values are reported for each (model × mechanism) pair in the Results scorecards

findings.mechanism: M2 — Dean-type secondary flows causing lateral hydrodynamic side-load at bends
findings.factor: Relevance of the quantities of interest
spans: Prototypes that showed hydrodynamic side-loads above 12 mN in the curvature rig were more likely to deviate from the wire in separate mechanical trackability tests that included wall contact and realistic friction; in a 24-run set, the correlation between peak hydrodynamic side-load and off-rail deviation rate was r = 0.78 (p < 0.001).
findings.span: Prototypes that showed hydrodynamic side-loads above 12 mN in the curvature rig were more likely to deviate from the wire in separate mechanical trackability tests that included wall contact and realistic friction; in a 24-run set, the correlation between peak hydrodynamic side-load and off-rail deviation rate was r = 0.78 (p < 0.001).

findings.span: A 6-axis force–torque sensor (resolution 0.2 mN, accuracy ±1% of reading) at the tip fixture recorded forces in the absence of wall contact except at designed glide pads with low friction (PTFE inserts) to isolate hydrodynamic side-loads from dry friction.
